Certify

/SER-tuh-fy/ — rhymes with modify · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To certify something is to officially confirm or provide proof that it is true, genuine, or meets a required standard.

The lab certified that the water was safe to drink.

Worked Example

Before the restaurant could open, the health inspector certified that all equipment met food safety standards, providing the official sign-off required by law.

Certify is more precise than 'checked' or 'confirmed' because it emphasizes the official, authoritative nature of the confirmation and the fact that something meets a required standard. Not just anyone can certify; an authority must officially verify the standard was met.

How Certify Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

verify

verify: to check carefully that something is true

confirm: to state that something is definitely true

validate: to officially declare something acceptable or sound

Antonyms

deny

deny: to declare that something is not true

invalidate

invalidate: to officially declare something void or unsound

How Strong Is It? — assume → verify → confirm → certify

assume vs. certify

assume vs. certify: Assume is the weakest word on this scale — assuming accepts something without any proof, while to certify is to officially guarantee it is true.

verify vs. certify

verify vs. certify: Verify is stronger than assume because verifying means actually checking the facts, but certify goes further by putting an official stamp of proof on them.

confirm vs. certify

confirm vs. certify: Confirm strengthens verify by declaring something true, yet certify tops them all: to certify is to confirm officially, with real authority and documentation behind it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cert

Root — cert: sure, settled, fixed (Latin (certus))

Suffix — -ify

Suffix — -ify: to make (Latin (-ficare, from facere 'to make, do'))

Put it together

Put it together: Cert- means 'sure or settled' and -ify means 'to make,' so to certify is literally 'to make sure' — to officially confirm that something is true, genuine, or up to the required standard.

Use the root in a new word: certain

Use the root in a new word: certain: After checking the map twice, Maya was certain of the route — 'certain' and 'certify' both grow from the same Latin root meaning 'sure.'

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Certify is a formal word used in official or professional contexts. Use it when something has been officially approved or proven to meet standards. For everyday checking, 'verify' or 'confirm' are simpler choices.
